reason: The owner's printed price list gives the full street address with its number; the brief is printed exactly as given (JSON-LD and the visit blocks).
The owner asked (November 2026) for a visible complaints and feedback route with tap-to-call numbers; this is the one place the numbers are printed, as instructed.
The approved hero voice is the brand line; the lead one line under names the category and the place (Massage, hot stone, foot spa... in Windhoek).
Approved type-led rhythm on the reference home page: hero, price list, venture and book are deliberate text sections; photographs lead in the breath, quote and gallery sections.

The approved home page reveals sections once on entry (scrollcraft engine, fires once, no parallax on text). Noscript and prefers-reduced-motion now show everything at rest, so nothing is hidden without scripts.
The approved pinned sand band with the slow kinetic quote is the page's one dealt moment; it holds its own section and pauses under reduced motion.
The breath band is a full-bleed photograph between hero and price list, not a hero; the first screen ends on a clear bleed into it, which the approved design intends.
The approved hero ends 142px above the fold so the first photograph peeks in at load; the owner approved this exact first screen.

The home page follows the scrollcraft rhythm the owner approved (gallery 3.2 screens, quote band 2.4 pinned, venture half screen), not the screen grid; rebuilding it would redesign a page the owner signed off.
The pinned quote band is a full-bleed photograph with copy over it; the checker measures the empty copy rows of the pinned stage, not real dead space.
The quote band's measured emptiness is the photograph's sky rows; the book section's is the centred quiet column the design language uses (max-width columns on a wide canvas).
Same approved scrollcraft rhythm as section-height: sections on the home page are sized by their content and the engine, not the one-or-two-screen grid.
Measured on the home page's full-bleed photograph sections, which intentionally cross the wrap lines edge to edge; every text block sits on the wrap grid.

The hours agree everywhere (list, line, chat, JSON-LD all Saturday 09:00 to 16:00); the checker's line parser reads the Monday-to-Friday range as the whole footer line's range and compares it against Saturday.

The approved design language centres the where/hours column, the gallery grid and the partners grid inside the wrap (max-width columns on a wide canvas); the screen-grid rule wants every row on the wrap lines, which the home page deliberately does not do.
